skill.name: git-analysis
skill.description: Analyze Git branch differences, commit history, changed files, and working tree state for pull requests and reviews.
skill.summary: Analyze Git changes and commit history for PR preparation, review, and commit planning.
skill.author: 1natsu172

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are expected git-analysis behavior, safe helper scripts, or Markdown command examples. The confirmed issue is a reference workflow that writes repository status and diffs to predictable /tmp/git_*.txt files. No prompt-injection text or malicious exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Predictable temporary files in reference examples
remediation.suggestion: Replace /tmp/git_*.txt examples with mktemp -d, store files inside that directory, set a cleanup trap, and restrict permissions.

remediation.issue: Advanced shell examples are less hardened than helper scripts
remediation.suggestion: Quote branch and merge-base variables consistently in documentation and direct users to the safer helper scripts for routine use.

content.value_statement: Reviewing branch changes can be slow when commits, diffs, and status are scattered. This skill gathers Git context for PRs, reviews, and commit planning.
actual_capabilities: Detects the default branch and merge base for branch comparisons.
Summarizes commits from the merge base to HEAD.
Reports changed files, insertions, deletions, and diff statistics.
Checks staged, unstaged, and untracked working tree changes.
Provides helper scripts for branch summaries and commit history.
Recommends output formats for PR and review workflows.
limitations: Requires a local Git repository and the git command-line tool.
Some workflows assume a remote named origin and a default branch reference.
Outputs may include sensitive branch names, file paths, commits, or diff details.
Does not authenticate to hosting services or create pull requests directly.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Summarize commits, changed files, and diff statistics before drafting a pull request.

use_cases.title: Review Feature Branches
use_cases.description: Compare a branch against its merge base to focus review effort.

use_cases.title: Audit Release Changes
use_cases.description: List commit history and file impact for release notes or team handoff.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize My Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Use git-analysis to summarize the current branch against the default branch. Include commit count, changed files, and main risks.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare PR Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this repository for a pull request. Group changes by area and list commits that need mention.

prompt_templates.title: Review Commit History
prompt_templates.prompt: Use git-analysis to inspect commits from the merge base to HEAD. Highlight unclear commits and review focus areas.

prompt_templates.title: Classify Branch Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a deep branch analysis. Classify changes by file type, connect commits to touched areas, and identify follow-up questions.

output_examples.input: Analyze the current feature branch before a pull request.
output_examples.output: Branch summary with base branch, merge base, commit count, changed files, and notable diffs.

output_examples.input: Review the commit history since divergence.
Compare staged and unstaged changes before committing.
output_examples.output: A working tree summary that separates staged changes, unstaged changes, and untracked files.

best_practices: Run from the repository root or clearly state the target repository path.
Review generated diffs before sharing because they may contain secrets.
Verify the detected default branch when repositories use nonstandard branch names.
anti_patterns: Do not run full diff analysis on repositories that contain secrets you cannot expose.
Do not assume origin/main when the repository reports a different default branch.
Do not use predictable temporary files from reference examples on shared systems.

faq.question: Does this skill change my repository?
faq.answer: The helper scripts read Git metadata and do not commit changes. Some reference examples write temporary files if copied directly.

faq.question: Does it need network access?
faq.answer: Most analysis is local. Checks that query origin may contact the configured remote.

faq.question: Can it create a pull request?
faq.answer: No. It prepares context that another workflow or user can use to draft a pull request.

faq.question: Does it work with Codex and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What data can appear in outputs?
faq.answer: Commit subjects, author metadata, branch names, file paths, and diff summaries can appear.

faq.question: How should I handle sensitive repositories?
faq.answer: Limit output scope, avoid full diffs, and review results before sharing outside the repository team.
